slides.text: A Go program is a text file with three parts: a package line, the packages it imports, and `func main`, where it starts. Here you type that skeleton, print your first lines, and meet the errors Go reports when a part is wrong.

intro.title: The shape of a Go file

slides.text: Every Go program answers three questions, always in this order. The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.
slides.code:
package    who am I?
import     what do I use?
func main  where do I start?

slides.text: You will type the code and run it with `go run main.go`. At the end of each exercise you see what the program prints.

exercises.title: Your first program
exercises.guide: Type the smallest Go program: it prints one line of text.

chunks.guide: Every Go file starts with its **package**. `main` is the package of a program you can run.

notes.text: A program you can run is always in package main.

chunks.guide: `import` brings in another package. `fmt` can print text.

notes.text: Short for format: it prints and formats text.

chunks.guide: `func main` is where the program starts. The braces hold what it does.
`Println` prints one line. The text goes between double quotes.

notes.text: Calls Println from the fmt package.

exercises.title: Import a package
exercises.guide: Import the package that `Println` comes from.

exercises.title: Print without a new line
exercises.guide: `Print` stays on the line and `Println` moves to the next. Use both.

chunks.guide: The package and the import are already in the file. `main` again.
`Print` writes the text and stays on the same line.

notes.text: Prints the text and stays on the same line.

chunks.guide: `Println` writes the text and then moves to the next line.

exercises.title: Why does it not compile?
exercises.guide: Read the message, then pick the cause.
options: The opening brace must be on the same line
`func` must be written with a capital
The braces must end with a semicolon
exercises.explanation: Go ends a line with an implicit semicolon, so a brace on its own line closes `func main()` too early. The opening brace stays on the same line.

exercises.title: Comments
exercises.guide: Add a comment, then print. Go ignores comments when it runs the program.

chunks.guide: The package and the import are already in the file. Type `main`.
`//` starts a comment: the rest of the line is ignored. Go also has `/* ... */` for several lines.

notes.text: Go ignores everything after this on the line.

chunks.guide: The comment changes nothing: the program prints as usual.

exercises.title: Two imports
exercises.guide: Import two packages in a block, and use both.

chunks.guide: With several packages, group them in parentheses, one per line. `strings` works with text.

notes.text: Imports several packages in one group.
A package of functions for working with text.

chunks.guide: `strings.ToUpper` turns text into capitals. It reads like `fmt.Println`: package, dot, function.

notes.text: Calls ToUpper from the strings package.

exercises.title: Complete the imports
exercises.guide: Import the package that `ToUpper` comes from.

exercises.title: What kind of error is it?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick the kind of error.
exercises.explanation: Go does not allow an import that the file never uses: it is a compile error.

exercises.title: Put it together
exercises.guide: Greet in three lines, with a comment. Statements run from top to bottom.

chunks.guide: The skeleton is already in the file. Start with a comment.
Lines run in the order they are written.
chunks.text: fmt.Println("This is my first Go program.")

output.text:
Hello!
This is my first Go program.
It runs top to bottom.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick the output.
exercises.code:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
    fmt.Print("a")
    fmt.Print("b")
    fmt.Println("c")
}
exercises.explanation: `Print` does not add a new line, so `a` and `b` stay on the line. `Println` adds `c` and then moves on.
